issues: The eye and beak are necessarily crowded at the far-left tip and lose a little separation at 1x.
The single magenta accent near the lower-right edge can momentarily read as an orphan pixel rather than a mechanical detail.
The raised wing's white interior dominates the body, slightly weakening the head-to-torso read.
fixes: Keep the beak tip and eye separated by at least one black contour pixel so their roles remain distinct at 1x.
Connect the lower-right magenta accent to the adjacent black or magenta cluster, or remove it if it is not an articulation marker.
If revising, trade one white wing-interior pixel for black along the wing root to clarify where the wing joins the body.

issues: The raised wing is extremely boxy and visually dominates the body, making it resemble a sail or tail at 1x.
The eye is a heavy rectangular black cluster without a pupil or highlight, reducing the usual Capcom facial charm.
The beak and forehead contain several competing single-pixel steps, making that area slightly cramped at true size.
The long black divisions across the belly and wing create more visual weight than typical MM2/MM3 interior detailing.
fixes: Remove one pixel from the wing's outer-right width and simplify its stepped feather edge into two clearer notches.
Replace one corner pixel of the black eye with white to create a crisp highlight while retaining its large size.
Simplify the beak to a clean two- or three-pixel wedge with an uninterrupted dark outline.
Shorten the interior black belly divider by one pixel and reconnect the surrounding white clusters for a lighter, rounder body.

issues: The eye-and-beak junction at the far left is slightly dense at 1x.
The isolated magenta pixels at the lower body and rear edge are less readable than the main clusters.
fixes: Simplify the beak junction by removing one dark pixel so the short beak separates more clearly from the eye.
Either connect each isolated magenta accent to a neighboring magenta pixel or remove it; keep the strong wing and body silhouette unchanged.

issues: The raised wing dominates the sprite as a broad white stepped slab, making the silhouette feel less lively than a Capcom MM2/MM3 flying enemy.
The eye and beak compress into a noisy cluster at the far-left head, so the advertised big eye is not immediately clear at 1x.
The lower body has a heavy, boxy black contour with an awkward rectangular notch near the center.
Single magenta accents at the wing tip and underside feel disconnected rather than forming deliberate highlight clusters.
The red beak introduces a near-redundant extra accent color alongside magenta.
fixes: Enlarge the eye to a clean 2x2 white cluster with one black pupil pixel, separated clearly from the beak.
Reduce the raised wing by one pixel along its right edge and reshape the outer contour into two or three decisive staircase steps.
Round the belly by moving the lower-left and lower-right outline pixels inward, removing the central rectangular notch.
Connect the underside magenta pixels into one compact 2-3-pixel shadow cluster or remove them.
Use the main magenta for the beak, or reserve the second red only if tile palette limits and sprite layering support it.
Add a one-pixel tail or rear-body break to distinguish wing, body, and tail more clearly at true size.

issues: The lower-center magenta stripe and tiny lower-right magenta accent are slightly ambiguous at 1x, reading more like isolated mechanical marks than clear anatomy.
The large raised wing visually outweighs the body, making the wing-to-torso joint a little difficult to parse.
The sprite appears marginally larger than the stated 18x16 target, though still plausible for a multi-tile NES enemy.
fixes: Join the lower-center magenta stripe more clearly to the body or remove one pixel so it reads as a deliberate tail or mechanical detail.
Clarify the wing joint by shifting one white pixel near its lower-left base to black or magenta, separating the wing from the torso.
If 18x16 is a strict limit, trim one pixel from the wing’s right edge and simplify the lower contour without altering the strong silhouette.
